learn.title: Same denominator
learn.body: When the denominators match, add or subtract only the numerators. $\frac{2}{5}+\frac{1}{5}=\frac{3}{5}$. The denominator stays, because the parts are still fifths. Simplify if you can.

learn.title: Different denominators
learn.body: You cannot add pieces of different sizes. First rewrite both fractions with a common denominator. Use the LCM of the denominators, so the numbers stay small. Then add the numerators.

learn.title: Work out $\frac{3}{4}-\frac{1}{3}$
learn.body: Subtracting works the same way. The LCM of 4 and 3 is 12.

learn.title: Answers bigger than one
learn.body: $\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2}{3}=\frac{3}{6}+\frac{4}{6}=\frac{7}{6}$. That is more than 1, so you can write it as the mixed number $1\frac{1}{6}$. Both forms are correct.
Never add the denominators. $\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}$ is 1, not $\frac{2}{4}$.

questions.explanation: The denominators match, so add only the numerators: $\frac{3}{5}$.

questions.prompt: To add fractions with different denominators, first find a \_\_ denominator.
questions.explanation: A common denominator lets you add parts of the same size. The LCM is the neatest choice.

questions.prompt: Work out $\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{4}$. Put the steps in order.
questions.explanation: Common denominator first, then add the tops.
